subject.title: [Bug] gateway shutdown timed out: node report shows active child process handle; leaves dirty shutdown + lane wait

question: Should normal SIGTERM/SIGINT gateway shutdown cancel active runs and their managed exec child processes, or preserve yielded/backgrounded exec sessions unless an explicit restart or process-kill path is used?
rationale: Current source and tests intentionally preserve active/background work on normal shutdown, so changing that behavior is an operator-safety and product-policy choice before it is a mechanical patch.

options.title: Define bounded managed-process shutdown
options.body: On normal stop, reject new work and cancel managed active run/exec scopes through the supervisor before the watchdog, with documented exceptions for any background process class maintainers choose to preserve.

options.title: Preserve current normal-stop behavior
options.body: Keep normal shutdown from aborting active/background exec work and treat this as a diagnostics or documentation issue instead of runtime cancellation behavior.

options.title: Defer to session exec-control design
options.body: Keep this open until https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/12554 defines the process-control contract, then reuse that contract for gateway shutdown.

recommendation.title: Define bounded managed-process shutdown
recommendation.body: On normal stop, reject new work and cancel managed active run/exec scopes through the supervisor before the watchdog, with documented exceptions for any background process class maintainers choose to preserve.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent has the strongest recent process/lane surface history among the likely owners and was already pulled into the issue timeline.
